# DBusInterfaceSkeleton in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusInterfaceSkeleton.html

`pub struct DBusInterfaceSkeleton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Abstract base class for D-Bus interfaces on the service side.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-flags)`g-flags`

Flags from the #GDBusInterfaceSkeletonFlags enumeration.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-authorize-method)`g-authorize-method`

Emitted when a method is invoked by a remote caller and used to determine if the method call is authorized.

Note that this signal is emitted in a thread dedicated to
handling the method call so handlers are allowed to perform
blocking IO. This means that it is appropriate to call e.g.
[polkit_authority_check_authorization_sync()](http://hal.freedesktop.org/docs/polkit/PolkitAuthority.html#polkit-authority-check-authorization-sync)
with the
[POLKIT_CHECK_AUTHORIZATION_FLAGS_ALLOW_USER_INTERACTION](http://hal.freedesktop.org/docs/polkit/PolkitAuthority.html#POLKIT-CHECK-AUTHORIZATION-FLAGS-ALLOW-USER-INTERACTION:CAPS)
flag set.

If [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) is returned then no further handlers are run and the
signal handler must take a reference to @invocation and finish
handling the call (e.g. return an error via
g_dbus_method_invocation_return_error()).

Otherwise, if [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) is returned, signal emission continues. If no
handlers return

[, then the method is dispatched. If @interface has an enclosing #GDBusObjectSkeleton, then the #GDBusObjectSkeleton::authorize-method signal handlers run before the handlers for this signal.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`The default class handler just returns [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html).

Please note that the common case is optimized: if no signals
handlers are connected and the default class handler isn’t
overridden (for both @interface and the enclosing
#GDBusObjectSkeleton, if any) and #GDBusInterfaceSkeleton:g-flags does
not have the
[ DBusInterfaceSkeletonFlags::HANDLE_METHOD_INVOCATIONS_IN_THREAD](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusInterfaceSkeletonFlags.html#associatedconstant.HANDLE_METHOD_INVOCATIONS_IN_THREAD)
flags set, no dedicated thread is ever used and the call will be
handled in the same thread as the object that @interface belongs
to was exported in.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[ DBusInterfaceSkeletonExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DBusInterfaceSkeletonExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`],

`DBusInterfaceExt`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

`GDBusMenuModel` is an implementation of [ MenuModel](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuModel.html) that can be

    object_path: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [DBusMenuModel](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMenuModel.html)

Obtains a #GDBusMenuModel for the menu model which is exported at the given @bus_name and @object_path.

The thread default main context is taken at the time of this call. All signals on the menu model (and any linked models) are reported with respect to this context. All calls on the returned menu model (and linked models) must also originate from this same context, with the thread default main context unchanged.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#connection)`connection`

a #GDBusConnection

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#bus_name)`bus_name`

the bus name which exports the menu model
or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if @connection is not a message bus connection

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#object_path)`object_path`

the object path at which the menu model is exported

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

a #GDBusMenuModel object. Free with g_object_unref().

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of

# MenuModel in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.MenuModel.html

`pub struct MenuModel { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GMenuModel` represents the contents of a menu — an ordered list of
menu items. The items are associated with actions, which can be
activated through them. Items can be grouped in sections, and may
have submenus associated with them. Both items and sections usually
have some representation data, such as labels or icons. The type of
the associated action (ie whether it is stateful, and what kind of
state it has) can influence the representation of the item.

The conceptual model of menus in `GMenuModel` is hierarchical:
sections and submenus are again represented by `GMenuModel`s.
Menus themselves do not define their own roles. Rather, the role
of a particular `GMenuModel` is defined by the item that references
it (or, in the case of the ‘root’ menu, is defined by the context
in which it is used).

As an example, consider the visible portions of this menu:

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#an-example-menu)An example menu

While this kind of deeply nested menu is no longer considered good UI
practice, it serves as a good example of the concepts in `GMenuModel`.
There are 8 ‘menus’ visible in the screenshot: one menubar, two
submenus and 5 sections:

- the toplevel menubar (containing 4 items)
- the View submenu (containing 3 sections)
- the first section of the View submenu (containing 2 items)
- the second section of the View submenu (containing 1 item)
- the final section of the View submenu (containing 1 item)
- the Highlight Mode submenu (containing 2 sections)
- the Sources section (containing 2 items)
- the Markup section (containing 2 items)

The [example](https://gtk-rs.org#a-menu-example) illustrates the conceptual connection between
these 8 menus. Each large block in the figure represents a menu and the
smaller blocks within the large block represent items in that menu. Some
items contain references to other menus.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#a-menu-example)A menu example

Notice that the separators visible in the [example](https://gtk-rs.org#an-example-menu)
appear nowhere in the [menu model](https://gtk-rs.org#a-menu-example). This is because
separators are not explicitly represented in the menu model. Instead,
a separator is inserted between any two non-empty sections of a menu.
Section items can have labels just like any other item. In that case,
a display system may show a section header instead of a separator.

The motivation for this abstract model of application controls is
that modern user interfaces tend to make these controls available
outside the application. Examples include global menus, jumplists,
dash boards, etc. To support such uses, it is necessary to ‘export’
information about actions and their representation in menus, which
is exactly what the action group exporter and the menu model exporter do for
[ ActionGroup](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ActionGroup.html) and

[. The client-side counterparts to make use of the exported information are](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuModel.html)

`MenuModel`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusActionGroup.html)

`DBusActionGroup`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMenuModel.html)

`DBusMenuModel`The API of `GMenuModel` is very generic, with iterators for the
attributes and links of an item, see
[ MenuModelExt::iterate_item_attributes()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.MenuModelExt.html#method.iterate_item_attributes) and

[. The ‘standard’ attributes and link types have predefined names:](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.MenuModelExt.html#method.iterate_item_links)

`MenuModelExt::iterate_item_links()``G_MENU_ATTRIBUTE_LABEL`,
`G_MENU_ATTRIBUTE_ACTION`, `G_MENU_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET`, `G_MENU_LINK_SECTION`
and `G_MENU_LINK_SUBMENU`.Items in a `GMenuModel` represent active controls if they refer to
an action that can get activated when the user interacts with the
menu item. The reference to the action is encoded by the string ID
in the `G_MENU_ATTRIBUTE_ACTION` attribute. An action ID uniquely
identifies an action in an action group. Which action group(s) provide
actions depends on the context in which the menu model is used.
E.g. when the model is exported as the application menu of a
[ GtkApplication](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Application.html),
actions can be application-wide or window-specific (and thus come from
two different action groups). By convention, the application-wide actions
have names that start with

`app.`, while the names of window-specific
actions start with `win.`.While a wide variety of stateful actions is possible, the following is the minimum that is expected to be supported by all users of exported menu information:

- an action with no parameter type and no state
- an action with no parameter type and boolean state
- an action with string parameter type and string state

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#stateless)Stateless

A stateless action typically corresponds to an ordinary menu item.

Selecting such a menu item will activate the action (with no parameter).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#boolean-state)Boolean State

An action with a boolean state will most typically be used with a ‘toggle’ or ‘switch’ menu item. The state can be set directly, but activating the action (with no parameter) results in the state being toggled.

Selecting a toggle menu item will activate the action. The menu item should be rendered as ‘checked’ when the state is true.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#string-parameter-and-state)String Parameter and State

Actions with string parameters and state will most typically be used to represent an enumerated choice over the items available for a group of radio menu items. Activating the action with a string parameter is equivalent to setting that parameter as the state.

Radio menu items, in addition to being associated with the action, will have a target value. Selecting that menu item will result in activation of the action with the target value as the parameter. The menu item should be rendered as ‘selected’ when the state of the action is equal to the target value of the menu item.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#items-changed)`items-changed`

Emitted when a change has occurred to the menu.

The only changes that can occur to a menu is that items are removed or added. Items may not change (except by being removed and added back in the same location). This signal is capable of describing both of those changes (at the same time).

The signal means that starting at the index @position, @removed items were removed and @added items were added in their place. If @removed is zero then only items were added. If @added is zero then only items were removed.

As an example, if the menu contains items a, b, c, d (in that order) and the signal (2, 1, 3) occurs then the new composition of the menu will be a, b, _, _, _, d (with each _ representing some new item).

Signal handlers may query the model (particularly the added items) and expect to see the results of the modification that is being reported. The signal is emitted after the modification.

`pub struct DBusMessage { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A type for representing D-Bus messages that can be sent or received
on a [ DBusConnection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusConnection.html).

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/dbus_message.rs.html#74-93)

#### pub fn [from_blob](https://gtk-rs.org#method.from_blob)(
    blob: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    capabilities: [DBusCapabilityFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusCapabilityFlags.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[DBusMessage](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMessage.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Creates a new D-Bus message from the data stored at @blob.

You must have previously called [ bytes_needed()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMessage.html#method.bytes_needed) on @blob,
and ensure that @blob is at least as long as the return value from that
function indicates. In particular, that means that @blob must be at least 16
bytes long (but will typically be much longer).

The byte order that the message was in can be retrieved using
[ byte_order()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMessage.html#method.byte_order).

If the @blob cannot be parsed, contains invalid fields, or contains invalid headers, [error@Gio.IOErrorEnum.INVALID_ARGUMENT] will be returned.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#blob)`blob`

a blob representing a binary D-Bus message

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#capabilities)`capabilities`

flags describing what protocol features are supported

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

The D-Bus message

Gets the UNIX file descriptors associated with @self, if any.

This method is only available on UNIX.

The file descriptors normally correspond to `G_VARIANT_TYPE_HANDLE`
values in the body of the message. For example, if
[`glib::Variant::handle()`][crate::glib::Variant::handle()] returns 5, that is intended to be a
reference to the file descriptor that can be accessed by
`g_unix_fd_list_get (list, 5, ...)`.

Flags:   none

Serial:  477

Body: ()
UNIX File Descriptors:
  fd 12: dev=0:10,mode=020620,ino=5,uid=500,gid=5,rdev=136:2,size=0,atime=1273085037,mtime=1273085851,ctime=1272982635

**Unix**only.

Sets the UNIX file descriptors associated with @self.

As a side-effect the [enum@Gio.DBusMessageHeaderField.NUM_UNIX_FDS] header
field is set to the number of fds in @fd_list (or cleared if
@fd_list is `NULL`).

This method is only available on UNIX.

When designing D-Bus APIs that are intended to be interoperable,
please note that non-GDBus implementations of D-Bus can usually only
access file descriptors if they are referenced by a value of type
`G_VARIANT_TYPE_HANDLE` in the body of the message.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#fd_list)`fd_list`

A [ UnixFDList](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.UnixFDList.html), or

`NULL` to clearSerializes @self to a blob.

The byte order returned by [ byte_order()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMessage.html#method.byte_order) will be
used.

calls `Gio::DBusError::set_dbus_error()` using the information in the

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of

# DBusMethodInvocation in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusMethodInvocation.html

`pub struct DBusMethodInvocation { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Instances of the `GDBusMethodInvocation` class are used when
handling D-Bus method calls. It provides a way to asynchronously
return results and errors.

The normal way to obtain a `GDBusMethodInvocation` object is to receive
it as an argument to the `handle_method_call()` function in a
[type@Gio.DBusInterfaceVTable] that was passed to
[ DBusConnection::register_object()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusConnection.html#method.register_object).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[`trait@glib::ObjectExt`]

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/dbus_method_invocation.rs.html#35-44)#### pub fn [return_error](https://gtk-rs.org#method.return_error)<T: [ErrorDomain](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/trait.ErrorDomain.html)>(&self, error: T, message: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/dbus_method_invocation.rs.html#35-44)

#### pub fn [return_error](https://gtk-rs.org#method.return_error)<T: [ErrorDomain](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/trait.ErrorDomain.html)>(&self, error: T, message: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Finishes handling a D-Bus method call by returning an error.

See g_dbus_error_encode_gerror() for details about what error name
will be returned on the wire. In a nutshell, if the given error is
registered using g_dbus_error_register_error() the name given
during registration is used. Otherwise, a name of the form
`org.gtk.GDBus.UnmappedGError.Quark...` is used. This provides
transparent mapping of #GError between applications using GDBus.

If you are writing an application intended to be portable, always register errors with g_dbus_error_register_error() or use g_dbus_method_invocation_return_dbus_error().

This method will take ownership of @self. See #GDBusInterfaceVTable for more information about the ownership of @self.

Since 2.48, if the method call requested for a reply not to be sent then this call will free @self but otherwise do nothing (as per the recommendations of the D-Bus specification).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#domain)`domain`

A #GQuark for the #GError error domain.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#code)`code`

The error code.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#format)`format`

printf()-style format.

Return a result for this invocation.

If `Ok` return the contained value with [ Self::return_value](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMethodInvocation.html#method.return_value).  If the return
value is not a tuple, automatically convert it to a one-element tuple, as
DBus return values must be tuples.

If `Err` return the contained error with [ Self::return_gerror](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMethodInvocation.html#method.return_gerror).

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/dbus_method_invocation.rs.html#95-102)#### pub fn [return_future_local](https://gtk-rs.org#method.return_future_local)<F>(self, f: F) -> [JoinHandle](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/main_context_futures/struct.JoinHandle.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/dbus_method_invocation.rs.html#95-102)

#### pub fn [return_future_local](https://gtk-rs.org#method.return_future_local)<F>(self, f: F) -> [JoinHandle](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/main_context_futures/struct.JoinHandle.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>

Return an async result for this invocation.

Spawn the given future on the thread-default main context, and return the
the result with [ Self::return_result](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusMethodInvocation.html#method.return_result).  Specifically, if a variant is returned
that is not a tuple it is automatically wrapped into a tuple.

The given `Future` does not have to be `Send`.

This can be called only from the thread where the main context is running, e.g.
from any other `Future` that is executed on this main context, or after calling
`with_thread_default` or `acquire` on the main context.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/dbus_method_invocation.rs.html#68-74)#### pub fn [interface_name](https://gtk-rs.org#method.interface_name)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[GString](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/gstring/struct.GString.html)>

Gets the name of the D-Bus interface the method was invoked on.

This can be `NULL` if it was not specified by the sender. See
`callback::Gio::DBusInterfaceMethodCallFunc or the
[D-Bus Specification](https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#message-protocol-types-method)
for details on when this can happen and how it should be handled.

If this method call is a property Get, Set or GetAll call that has been redirected to the method call handler then “org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties” will be returned. See #GDBusInterfaceVTable for more information.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/dbus_method_invocation.rs.html#283-290)#### pub fn [return_value](https://gtk-rs.org#method.return_value)(self, parameters: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[Variant](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/variant/struct.Variant.html)>)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/dbus_method_invocation.rs.html#283-290)

#### pub fn [return_value](https://gtk-rs.org#method.return_value)(self, parameters: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[Variant](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/variant/struct.Variant.html)>)

Finishes handling a D-Bus method call by returning @parameters. If the @parameters GVariant is floating, it is consumed.

It is an error if @parameters is not of the right format: it must be a tuple
containing the out-parameters of the D-Bus method. Even if the method has a
single out-parameter, it must be contained in a tuple. If the method has no
out-parameters, @parameters may be [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) or an empty tuple.

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
GDBusMethodInvocation *invocation = some_invocation;
g_autofree gchar *result_string = NULL;
g_autoptr (GError) error = NULL;
result_string = calculate_result (&error);
if (error != NULL)
  g_dbus_method_invocation_return_gerror (invocation, error);
else
  g_dbus_method_invocation_return_value (invocation,
                                         g_variant_new ("(s)", result_string));
// Do not free @self here; returning a value does that
```
This method will take ownership of @self. See #GDBusInterfaceVTable for more information about the ownership of @self.

Since 2.48, if the method call requested for a reply not to be sent then this call will sink @parameters and free @self, but otherwise do nothing (as per the recommendations of the D-Bus specification).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#parameters)`parameters`

A #GVariant tuple with out parameters for the method or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if not passing any parameters.

# DBusNodeInfo in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusNodeInfo.html

`pub struct DBusNodeInfo { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Information about nodes in a remote object hierarchy.

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/dbus_node_info.rs.html#20-73)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#impl-DBusNodeInfo-2)### impl [DBusNodeInfo](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusNodeInfo.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/dbus_node_info.rs.html#20-73)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#impl-DBusNodeInfo-2)

### impl [DBusNodeInfo](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusNodeInfo.html)

Parses @xml_data and returns a #GDBusNodeInfo representing the data.

The introspection XML must contain exactly one top-level
`<node>` element.

Note that this routine is using a
[GMarkup](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/markup.html)-based
parser that only accepts a subset of valid XML documents.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#xml_data)`xml_data`

Valid D-Bus introspection XML.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

A #GDBusNodeInfo structure or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if @error is set. Free
with g_dbus_node_info_unref().

# DBusObject in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusObject.html

`pub struct DBusObject { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The `GDBusObject` type is the base type for D-Bus objects on both
the service side (see [ DBusObjectSkeleton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectSkeleton.html)) and the client side
(see

[). It is essentially just a container of interfaces.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectProxy.html)

`DBusObjectProxy`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-added)`interface-added`

Emitted when @interface is added to @object.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-removed)`interface-removed`

Emitted when @interface is removed from @object.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# DBusObjectSkeleton in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusObjectSkeleton.html

`pub struct DBusObjectSkeleton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A `GDBusObjectSkeleton` instance is essentially a group of D-Bus
interfaces. The set of exported interfaces on the object may be
dynamic and change at runtime.

This type is intended to be used with [ DBusObjectManager](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-object-path)`g-object-path`

The object path where the object is exported.

Readable | Writable | Construct

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#authorize-method)`authorize-method`

Emitted when a method is invoked by a remote caller and used to determine if the method call is authorized.

This signal is like #GDBusInterfaceSkeleton’s #GDBusInterfaceSkeleton::g-authorize-method signal, except that it is for the enclosing object.

The default class handler just returns [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html).

#### DBusObject

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-added)`interface-added`

Emitted when @interface is added to @object.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-removed)`interface-removed`

Emitted when @interface is removed from @object.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`],

# DBusObjectProxy in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusObjectProxy.html

`pub struct DBusObjectProxy { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A `GDBusObjectProxy` is an object used to represent a remote object
with one or more D-Bus interfaces. Normally, you don’t instantiate
a `GDBusObjectProxy` yourself — typically [ DBusObjectManagerClient](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html)
is used to obtain it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-connection)`g-connection`

The connection of the proxy.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-object-path)`g-object-path`

The object path of the proxy.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#method.watch_closure)

#### fn [watch_closure](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.ObjectExt.html#tymethod.watch_closure)(&self, closure: &impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Closure](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/closure/struct.Closure.html)>)

`closure` to the lifetime of the object. When
the object’s reference count drops to zero, the closure will be
invalidated. An invalidated closure will ignore any calls to

# DBusObjectManager in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusObjectManager.html

`pub struct DBusObjectManager { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The `GDBusObjectManager` type is the base type for service- and
client-side implementations of the standardized
[ org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager](http://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#standard-interfaces-objectmanager)
interface.

See [ DBusObjectManagerClient](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html) for the client-side implementation
and

[for the service-side implementation.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerServer.html)

`DBusObjectManagerServer`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-added)`interface-added`

Emitted when @interface is added to @object.

This signal exists purely as a convenience to avoid having to connect signals to all objects managed by @manager.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-removed)`interface-removed`

Emitted when @interface has been removed from @object.

This signal exists purely as a convenience to avoid having to connect signals to all objects managed by @manager.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#object-added)`object-added`

Emitted when @object is added to @manager.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#object-removed)`object-removed`

Emitted when @object is removed from @manager.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# DBusObjectManagerClient in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html

`pub struct DBusObjectManagerClient { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GDBusObjectManagerClient` is used to create, monitor and delete object
proxies for remote objects exported by a [ DBusObjectManagerServer](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerServer.html)
(or any code implementing the

[org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager](http://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#standard-interfaces-objectmanager)interface).

Once an instance of this type has been created, you can connect to
the [ object-added](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html#object-added) and

[signals] and inspect the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html#object-removed)

`object-removed`[objects returned by](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectProxy.html)

`DBusObjectProxy`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DBusObjectManagerExt.html#method.objects)

`DBusObjectManagerExt::objects()`If the name for a `GDBusObjectManagerClient` is not owned by anyone at
object construction time, the default behavior is to request the
message bus to launch an owner for the name. This behavior can be
disabled using the `G_DBUS_OBJECT_MANAGER_CLIENT_FLAGS_DO_NOT_AUTO_START`
flag. It’s also worth noting that this only works if the name of
interest is activatable in the first place. E.g. in some cases it
is not possible to launch an owner for the requested name. In this
case, `GDBusObjectManagerClient` object construction still succeeds but
there will be no object proxies
(e.g. [ DBusObjectManagerExt::objects()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DBusObjectManagerExt.html#method.objects) returns the empty list) and
the

[property is](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#name-owner)

`name-owner``NULL`.The owner of the requested name can come and go (for example
consider a system service being restarted) – `GDBusObjectManagerClient`
handles this case too; simply connect to the [ notify](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/struct.Object.html#notify)
signal to watch for changes on the

[property. When the name owner vanishes, the behavior is that](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#name-owner)

`name-owner`[is set to](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#name-owner)

`name-owner``NULL` (this
includes emission of the [signal) and then](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/struct.Object.html#notify)

`notify`[signals are synthesized for all currently existing object proxies. Since](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html#object-removed)

`object-removed`[is](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#name-owner)

`name-owner``NULL` when this
happens, you can use this information to disambiguate a synthesized signal
from a genuine signal caused by object removal on the remote
[. Similarly, when a new name owner appears,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html)

`DBusObjectManager`[signals are synthesized while](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html#object-added)

`object-added`[is still](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#name-owner)

`name-owner``NULL`. Only
when all object proxies have been added, the
[is set to the new name owner (this includes emission of the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#name-owner)

`name-owner`[signal). Furthermore, you are guaranteed that](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/struct.Object.html#notify)

`notify`[will alternate between a name owner (e.g.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#name-owner)

`name-owner``:1.42`) and `NULL` even in the case where
the name of interest is atomically replacedUltimately, `GDBusObjectManagerClient` is used to obtain
[ DBusProxy](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html) instances. All signals (including the

`org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties::PropertiesChanged` signal)
delivered to [instances are guaranteed to originate from the name owner. This guarantee along with the behavior described above, means that certain race conditions including the “half the proxy is from the old owner and the other half is from the new owner” problem cannot happen.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html)

`DBusProxy`To avoid having the application connect to signals on the returned
[ DBusObjectProxy](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectProxy.html) and

[objects, the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html)

`DBusProxy`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObject.html#interface-added)

`interface-added`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObject.html#interface-removed)

`interface-removed`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-properties-changed)

`g-properties-changed`[signals are also emitted on the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-signal)

`g-signal``GDBusObjectManagerClient` instance managing these
objects. The signals emitted are
[,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html#interface-added)

`interface-added`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManager.html#interface-removed)

`interface-removed`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#interface-proxy-properties-changed)

`interface-proxy-properties-changed`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html#interface-proxy-signal)

`interface-proxy-signal`Note that all callbacks and signals are emitted in the
thread-default main context (see
[`glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()]) that the
`GDBusObjectManagerClient` object was constructed in. Additionally, the
[ DBusObjectProxy](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectProxy.html) and

[objects originating from the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html)

`DBusProxy``GDBusObjectManagerClient` object will be created in
the same context and, consequently, will deliver signals in the
same main loop.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-proxy-properties-changed)`interface-proxy-properties-changed`

Emitted when one or more D-Bus properties on proxy changes. The
local cache has already been updated when this signal fires. Note
that both @changed_properties and @invalidated_properties are
guaranteed to never be [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) (either may be empty though).

This signal exists purely as a convenience to avoid having to connect signals to all interface proxies managed by @manager.

This signal is emitted in the thread-default main context
(see [`glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()])
that @manager was constructed in.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interface-proxy-signal)`interface-proxy-signal`

Emitted when a D-Bus signal is received on @interface_proxy.

This signal exists purely as a convenience to avoid having to connect signals to all interface proxies managed by @manager.

This signal is emitted in the thread-default main context
(see [`glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()])
that @manager was constructed in.

#### DBusObjectManager

#### pub fn [new](https://gtk-rs.org#method.new)<P: [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)([Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[DBusObjectManagerClient](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) + 'static>(
    connection: &[DBusConnection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusConnection.html),

Asynchronously creates a new #GDBusObjectManagerClient object.

This is an asynchronous failable constructor. When the result is
ready, @callback will be invoked in the thread-default main context
(see [`glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()])
of the thread you are calling this method from. You can then call
g_dbus_object_manager_client_new_finish() to get the result. See
g_dbus_object_manager_client_new_sync() for the synchronous version.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#connection-1)`connection`

A #GDBusConnection.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#flags-1)`flags`

Zero or more flags from the #GDBusObjectManagerClientFlags enumeration.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#name-1)`name`

The owner of the control object (unique or well-known name).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#object_path)`object_path`

The object path of the control object.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#get_proxy_type_func)`get_proxy_type_func`

A #GDBusProxyTypeFunc function or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) to always construct #GDBusProxy proxies.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#get_proxy_type_user_data)`get_proxy_type_user_data`

User data to pass to @get_proxy_type_func.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#get_proxy_type_destroy_notify)`get_proxy_type_destroy_notify`

Free function for @get_proxy_type_user_data or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None).

A #GCancellable or `None`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#callback)`callback`

A #GAsyncReadyCallback to call when the request is satisfied.

and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of

# DBusObjectManagerServer in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusObjectManagerServer.html

`pub struct DBusObjectManagerServer { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GDBusObjectManagerServer` is used to export [ DBusObject](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObject.html) instances
using the standardized

[interface. For example, remote D-Bus clients can get all objects and properties in a single call. Additionally, any change in the object hierarchy is broadcast using signals. This means that D-Bus clients can keep caches up to date by only listening to D-Bus signals.](http://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#standard-interfaces-objectmanager)

`org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager`The recommended path to export an object manager at is the path form of the
well-known name of a D-Bus service, or below. For example, if a D-Bus service
is available at the well-known name `net.example.ExampleService1`, the object
manager should typically be exported at `/net/example/ExampleService1`, or
below (to allow for multiple object managers in a service).

It is supported, but not recommended, to export an object manager at the root
path, `/`.

See [ DBusObjectManagerClient](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerClient.html) for the client-side code that is
intended to be used with

`GDBusObjectManagerServer` or any D-Bus
object implementing the `org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager` interface.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#connection)`connection`

The #GDBusConnection to export objects on.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#object-path)`object-path`

The object path to register the manager object at.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[ DBusObjectManagerServerExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DBusObjectManagerServerExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`],

`DBusObjectManagerExt`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

#### pub fn [new](https://gtk-rs.org#method.new)(object_path: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [DBusObjectManagerServer](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusObjectManagerServer.html)

Creates a new #GDBusObjectManagerServer object.

The returned server isn’t yet exported on any connection. To do so,
use g_dbus_object_manager_server_set_connection(). Normally you
want to export all of your objects before doing so to avoid
[InterfacesAdded](http://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#standard-interfaces-objectmanager)
signals being emitted.

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# DBusProxy in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DBusProxy.html

`pub struct DBusProxy { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GDBusProxy` is a base class used for proxies to access a D-Bus
interface on a remote object. A `GDBusProxy` can be constructed for
both well-known and unique names.

By default, `GDBusProxy` will cache all properties (and listen to
changes) of the remote object, and proxy all signals that get
emitted. This behaviour can be changed by passing suitable
[ DBusProxyFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html) when the proxy is created. If the proxy is for a
well-known name, the property cache is flushed when the name owner
vanishes and reloaded when a name owner appears.

The unique name owner of the proxy’s name is tracked and can be read from
[ g-name-owner](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-name-owner). Connect to the

[signal to get notified of changes. Additionally, only signals and property changes emitted from the current name owner are considered and calls are always sent to the current name owner. This avoids a number of race conditions when the name is lost by one owner and claimed by another. However, if no name owner currently exists, then calls will be sent to the well-known name which may result in the message bus launching an owner (unless](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/struct.Object.html#notify)

`notify``G_DBUS_PROXY_FLAGS_DO_NOT_AUTO_START` is set).If the proxy is for a stateless D-Bus service, where the name owner may
be started and stopped between calls, the
[ g-name-owner](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-name-owner) tracking of

`GDBusProxy` will cause the
proxy to drop signal and property changes from the service after it has
restarted for the first time. When interacting with a stateless D-Bus
service, do not use `GDBusProxy` — use direct D-Bus method calls and signal
connections.The generic [ g-properties-changed](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-properties-changed) and

[signals are not very convenient to work with. Therefore, the recommended way of working with proxies is to subclass](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-signal)

`g-signal``GDBusProxy`, and have more natural properties and signals in your derived
class. This [example](https://gtk-rs.org/migrating-gdbus.html#using-gdbus-codegen)shows how this can easily be done using the

[tool.](https://gtk-rs.org/gdbus-codegen.html)

`gdbus-codegen`A `GDBusProxy` instance can be used from multiple threads but note
that all signals (e.g. [ g-signal](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-signal),

[and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html#g-properties-changed)

`g-properties-changed`[) are emitted in the thread-default main context (see [](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/struct.Object.html#notify)

`notify``glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()]) of the thread
where the instance was constructed.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#a-watch-proxy-example)A watch proxy example

An example using a proxy for a well-known name can be found in
[ gdbus-example-watch-proxy.c](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/blob/HEAD/gio/tests/gdbus-example-watch-proxy.c).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-bus-type)`g-bus-type`

If this property is not [ BusType::None](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.BusType.html#variant.None), then
#GDBusProxy:g-connection must be

[and will be set to the #GDBusConnection obtained by calling g_bus_get() with the value of this property.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-connection)`g-connection`

The #GDBusConnection the proxy is for.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-default-timeout)`g-default-timeout`

The timeout to use if -1 (specifying default timeout) is passed as @timeout_msec in the g_dbus_proxy_call() and g_dbus_proxy_call_sync() functions.

This allows applications to set a proxy-wide timeout for all
remote method invocations on the proxy. If this property is -1,
the default timeout (typically 25 seconds) is used. If set to
`G_MAXINT`, then no timeout is used.

Readable | Writable | Construct

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-flags)`g-flags`

Flags from the #GDBusProxyFlags enumeration.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-interface-info)`g-interface-info`

Ensure that interactions with this proxy conform to the given interface. This is mainly to ensure that malformed data received from the other peer is ignored. The given #GDBusInterfaceInfo is said to be the “expected interface”.

The checks performed are:

-
When completing a method call, if the type signature of the reply message isn’t what’s expected, the reply is discarded and the #GError is set to `IOErrorEnum::InvalidArgument`
-
Received signals that have a type signature mismatch are dropped and a warning is logged via g_warning().
-
Properties received via the initial `GetAll()`call or via the`::PropertiesChanged`signal (on the[org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties](http://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#standard-interfaces-properties)interface) or set using g_dbus_proxy_set_cached_property() with a type signature mismatch are ignored and a warning is logged via g_warning().

Note that these checks are never done on methods, signals and properties that are not referenced in the given #GDBusInterfaceInfo, since extending a D-Bus interface on the service-side is not considered an ABI break.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-interface-name)`g-interface-name`

The D-Bus interface name the proxy is for.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-name)`g-name`

The well-known or unique name that the proxy is for.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-name-owner)`g-name-owner`

The unique name that owns #GDBusProxy:g-name or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if no-one
currently owns that name. You may connect to #GObject::notify signal to
track changes to this property.

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-object-path)`g-object-path`

The object path the proxy is for.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-properties-changed)`g-properties-changed`

Emitted when one or more D-Bus properties on @proxy changes. The
local cache has already been updated when this signal fires. Note
that both @changed_properties and @invalidated_properties are
guaranteed to never be [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) (either may be empty though).

If the proxy has the flag
[ DBusProxyFlags::GET_INVALIDATED_PROPERTIES](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.GET_INVALIDATED_PROPERTIES) set, then
@invalidated_properties will always be empty.

This signal corresponds to the
`PropertiesChanged` D-Bus signal on the
`org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties` interface.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#g-signal)`g-signal`

Emitted when a signal from the remote object and interface that @proxy is for, has been received.

Since 2.72 this signal supports detailed connections. You can connect to
the detailed signal `g-signal::x` in order to receive callbacks only when
signal `x` is received from the remote object.

Detailed

#### pub fn [new_sync](https://gtk-rs.org#method.new_sync)(
    connection: &[DBusConnection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusConnection.html),
    flags: [DBusProxyFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html),
    info: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[DBusInterfaceInfo](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusInterfaceInfo.html)>,
    name: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>,
    object_path: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    interface_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Cancellable.html)>>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[DBusProxy](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Creates a proxy for accessing @interface_name on the remote object
at @object_path owned by @name at @connection and synchronously
loads D-Bus properties unless the
[ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES) flag is used.

If the [ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS) flag is not set, also sets up
match rules for signals. Connect to the #GDBusProxy::g-signal signal
to handle signals from the remote object.

If both [ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES) and

[are set, this constructor is guaranteed to return immediately without blocking.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS)

`DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS`If @name is a well-known name and the
[ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_AUTO_START](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_AUTO_START) and

[flags aren’t set and no name owner currently exists, the message bus will be requested to launch a name owner for the name.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_AUTO_START_AT_CONSTRUCTION)

`DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_AUTO_START_AT_CONSTRUCTION`This is a synchronous failable constructor. See g_dbus_proxy_new() and g_dbus_proxy_new_finish() for the asynchronous version.

#GDBusProxy is used in this [example](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html)[crate::DBusProxy](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html)#a-watch-proxy-example].

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#info-1)`info`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#name-1)`name`

Creates a proxy for accessing @interface_name on the remote object
at @object_path owned by @name at @connection and asynchronously
loads D-Bus properties unless the
[ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES) flag is used. Connect to
the #GDBusProxy::g-properties-changed signal to get notified about
property changes.

If the [ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS) flag is not set, also sets up
match rules for signals. Connect to the #GDBusProxy::g-signal signal
to handle signals from the remote object.

If both [ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_LOAD_PROPERTIES) and

[are set, this constructor is guaranteed to complete immediately without blocking.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS)

`DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_CONNECT_SIGNALS`If @name is a well-known name and the
[ DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_AUTO_START](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_AUTO_START) and

[flags aren’t set and no name owner currently exists, the message bus will be requested to launch a name owner for the name.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxyFlags.html#associatedconstant.DO_NOT_AUTO_START_AT_CONSTRUCTION)

`DBusProxyFlags::DO_NOT_AUTO_START_AT_CONSTRUCTION`This is a failable asynchronous constructor - when the proxy is ready, @callback will be invoked and you can use g_dbus_proxy_new_finish() to get the result.

See g_dbus_proxy_new_sync() and for a synchronous version of this constructor.

#GDBusProxy is used in this [example](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html)[crate::DBusProxy](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DBusProxy.html)#a-watch-proxy-example].

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

#### pub const [GET_INVALIDATED_PROPERTIES](https://gtk-rs.org#associatedconstant.GET_INVALIDATED_PROPERTIES): Self

If set, the property value for any **invalidated property** will be (asynchronously) retrieved upon receiving the [ PropertiesChanged](http://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#standard-interfaces-properties) D-Bus signal and the property will not cause emission of the #GDBusProxy::g-properties-changed signal. When the value is received the #GDBusProxy::g-properties-changed signal is emitted for the property along with the retrieved value. Since 2.32.

Flags used when subscribing to signals via g_dbus_connection_signal_subscribe().

#### fn [sub_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/arith/trait.SubAssign.html#tymethod.sub_assign)(&mut self, other: Self)

The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# DataInputStream in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DataInputStream.html

`pub struct DataInputStream { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Data input stream implements [ InputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InputStream.html) and includes functions
for reading structured data directly from a binary input stream.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#byte-order)`byte-order`

The :byte-order property determines the byte ordering that is used when reading multi-byte entities (such as integers) from the stream.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#newline-type)`newline-type`

The :newline-type property determines what is considered as a line ending when reading complete lines from the stream.

Readable | Writable

#### BufferedInputStream

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#buffer-size)`buffer-size`

The size of the backend buffer, in bytes.

Readable | Writable | Construct

#### FilterInputStream

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#base-stream)`base-stream`

The underlying base stream on which the I/O ops will be done.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#close-base-stream)`close-base-stream`

Whether the base stream should be closed when the filter stream is closed.

Readable | Writable | Construct

# DataOutputStream in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DataOutputStream.html

`pub struct DataOutputStream { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Data output stream implements [ OutputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.OutputStream.html) and includes functions
for writing data directly to an output stream.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#byte-order)`byte-order`

Determines the byte ordering that is used when writing multi-byte entities (such as integers) to the stream.

Readable | Writable

#### FilterOutputStream

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#base-stream)`base-stream`

The underlying base stream on which the I/O ops will be done.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#close-base-stream)`close-base-stream`

Whether the base stream should be closed when the filter stream is closed.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

# DatagramBased in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DatagramBased.html

`pub struct DatagramBased { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Interface for socket-like objects with datagram semantics.

A `GDatagramBased` is a networking interface for representing datagram-based
communications. It is a more or less direct mapping of the core parts of the
BSD socket API in a portable GObject interface. It is implemented by
[ Socket](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Socket.html), which wraps the UNIX socket API on UNIX and winsock2 on Windows.

`GDatagramBased` is entirely platform independent, and is intended to be used
alongside higher-level networking APIs such as [ IOStream](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IOStream.html).

It uses vectored scatter/gather I/O by default, allowing for many messages
to be sent or received in a single call. Where possible, implementations of
the interface should take advantage of vectored I/O to minimise processing
or system calls. For example, `GSocket` uses `recvmmsg()` and `sendmmsg()`
where possible. Callers should take advantage of scatter/gather I/O (the use of
multiple buffers per message) to avoid unnecessary copying of data to
assemble or disassemble a message.

Each `GDatagramBased` operation has a timeout parameter which may be negative
for blocking behaviour, zero for non-blocking behaviour, or positive for
timeout behaviour. A blocking operation blocks until finished or there is an
error. A non-blocking operation will return immediately with a
`G_IO_ERROR_WOULD_BLOCK` error if it cannot make progress. A timeout operation
will block until the operation is complete or the timeout expires; if the
timeout expires it will return what progress it made, or
`G_IO_ERROR_TIMED_OUT` if no progress was made. To know when a call would
successfully run you can call [ DatagramBasedExt::condition_check()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DatagramBasedExt.html#method.condition_check) or

[. You can also use](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DatagramBasedExtManual.html#method.condition_wait)

`DatagramBasedExtManual::condition_wait()`[and attach it to a](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DatagramBasedExtManual.html#method.create_source)

`DatagramBasedExtManual::create_source()`[to get callbacks when I/O is possible.](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/auto/main_context/struct.MainContext.html)

`glib::MainContext`When running a non-blocking operation applications should always be able to
handle getting a `G_IO_ERROR_WOULD_BLOCK` error even when some other function
said that I/O was possible. This can easily happen in case of a race
condition in the application, but it can also happen for other reasons. For
instance, on Windows a socket is always seen as writable until a write
returns `G_IO_ERROR_WOULD_BLOCK`.

As with `GSocket`, `GDatagramBased`s can be either connection oriented (for
example, SCTP) or connectionless (for example, UDP). `GDatagramBased`s must be
datagram-based, not stream-based. The interface does not cover connection
establishment — use methods on the underlying type to establish a connection
before sending and receiving data through the `GDatagramBased` API. For
connectionless socket types the target/source address is specified or
received in each I/O operation.

Like most other APIs in GLib, `GDatagramBased` is not inherently thread safe.
To use a `GDatagramBased` concurrently from multiple threads, you must
implement your own locking.

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# DebugController in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DebugController.html

`pub struct DebugController { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`v2_72`## Expand description

`GDebugController` is an interface to expose control of debugging features and
debug output.

It is implemented on Linux using [ DebugControllerDBus](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DebugControllerDBus.html), which
exposes a D-Bus interface to allow authenticated peers to control debug
features in this process.

Whether debug output is enabled is exposed as
[ debug-enabled](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DebugController.html#debug-enabled). This controls

`log_set_debug_enabled()` by default. Application code may
connect to the [signal for it to control other parts of its debug infrastructure as necessary.](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/struct.Object.html#notify)

`notify`If your application or service is using the default GLib log writer function,
creating one of the built-in implementations of `GDebugController` should be
all that’s needed to dynamically enable or disable debug output.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#debug-enabled)`debug-enabled`

[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if debug output should be exposed (for example by forwarding it to
the journal),

[otherwise.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[ DebugControllerExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DebugControllerExt.html),

`InitableExt`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# DebugControllerDBus in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DebugControllerDBus.html

`pub struct DebugControllerDBus { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`v2_72`## Expand description

`GDebugControllerDBus` is an implementation of [ DebugController](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DebugController.html)
which exposes debug settings as a D-Bus object.

It is a [ Initable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Initable.html) object, and will register an object at

`/org/gtk/Debugging` on the bus given as
[once it’s initialized. The object will be unregistered when the last reference to the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DebugControllerDBus.html#connection)

`connection``GDebugControllerDBus` is dropped.This D-Bus object can be used by remote processes to enable or disable debug
output in this process. Remote processes calling
`org.gtk.Debugging.SetDebugEnabled()` will affect the value of
[ debug-enabled](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DebugController.html#debug-enabled) and, by default,

`log_get_debug_enabled()`.By default, no processes are allowed to call `SetDebugEnabled()` unless a
[ authorize](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DebugControllerDBus.html#authorize) signal handler is installed. This
is because the process may be privileged, or might expose sensitive
information in its debug output. You may want to restrict the ability to
enable debug output to privileged users or processes.

One option is to install a D-Bus security policy which restricts access to
`SetDebugEnabled()`, installing something like the following in
`$datadir/dbus-1/system.d/`:

```
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE busconfig PUBLIC "-//freedesktop//DTD D-BUS Bus Configuration 1.0//EN"
     "http://www.freedesktop.org/standards/dbus/1.0/busconfig.dtd">
<busconfig>
  <policy user="root">
    <allow send_destination="com.example.MyService" send_interface="org.gtk.Debugging"/>
  </policy>
  <policy context="default">
    <deny send_destination="com.example.MyService" send_interface="org.gtk.Debugging"/>
  </policy>
</busconfig>
```
This will prevent the `SetDebugEnabled()` method from being called by all
except root. It will not prevent the `DebugEnabled` property from being read,
as it’s accessed through the `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties` interface.

Another option is to use polkit to allow or deny requests on a case-by-case
basis, allowing for the possibility of dynamic authorisation. To do this,
connect to the [ authorize](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DebugControllerDBus.html#authorize) signal and query
polkit in it:

**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

```
  g_autoptr(GError) child_error = NULL;
  g_autoptr(GDBusConnection) connection = g_bus_get_sync (G_BUS_TYPE_SYSTEM, NULL, NULL);
  gulong debug_controller_authorize_id = 0;
  // Set up the debug controller.
  debug_controller = G_DEBUG_CONTROLLER (g_debug_controller_dbus_new (priv->connection, NULL, &child_error));
  if (debug_controller == NULL)
    {
      g_error ("Could not register debug controller on bus: %s",
               child_error->message);
    }
  debug_controller_authorize_id = g_signal_connect (debug_controller,
                                                    "authorize",
                                                    G_CALLBACK (debug_controller_authorize_cb),
                                                    self);
  static gboolean
  debug_controller_authorize_cb (GDebugControllerDBus  *debug_controller,
                                 GDBusMethodInvocation *invocation,
                                 gpointer               user_data)
  {
    g_autoptr(PolkitAuthority) authority = NULL;
    g_autoptr(PolkitSubject) subject = NULL;
    g_autoptr(PolkitAuthorizationResult) auth_result = NULL;
    g_autoptr(GError) local_error = NULL;
    GDBusMessage *message;
    GDBusMessageFlags message_flags;
    PolkitCheckAuthorizationFlags flags = POLKIT_CHECK_AUTHORIZATION_FLAGS_NONE;
    message = g_dbus_method_invocation_get_message (invocation);
    message_flags = g_dbus_message_get_flags (message);
    authority = polkit_authority_get_sync (NULL, &local_error);
    if (authority == NULL)
      {
        g_warning ("Failed to get polkit authority: %s", local_error->message);
        return FALSE;
      }
    if (message_flags & G_DBUS_MESSAGE_FLAGS_ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION)
      flags |= POLKIT_CHECK_AUTHORIZATION_FLAGS_ALLOW_USER_INTERACTION;
    subject = polkit_system_bus_name_new (g_dbus_method_invocation_get_sender (invocation));
    auth_result = polkit_authority_check_authorization_sync (authority,
                                                             subject,
                                                             "com.example.MyService.set-debug-enabled",
                                                             NULL,
                                                             flags,
                                                             NULL,
                                                             &local_error);
    if (auth_result == NULL)
      {
        g_warning ("Failed to get check polkit authorization: %s", local_error->message);
        return FALSE;
      }
    return polkit_authorization_result_get_is_authorized (auth_result);
  }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#connection)`connection`

The D-Bus connection to expose the debugging interface on.

Typically this will be the same connection (to the system or session bus) which the rest of the application or service’s D-Bus objects are registered on.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

#### DebugController

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#debug-enabled)`debug-enabled`

[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if debug output should be exposed (for example by forwarding it to
the journal),

[otherwise.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#authorize)`authorize`

Emitted when a D-Bus peer is trying to change the debug settings and used to determine if that is authorized.

This signal is emitted in a dedicated worker thread, so handlers are
allowed to perform blocking I/O. This means that, for example, it is
appropriate to call `polkit_authority_check_authorization_sync()` to check
authorization using polkit.

If [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) is returned then no further handlers are run and the request to
change the debug settings is rejected.

Otherwise, if [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) is returned, signal emission continues. If no handlers
return

[, then the debug settings are allowed to be changed.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`Signal handlers must not modify @invocation, or cause it to return a value.

The default class handler just returns [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html).

Create a new #GDebugControllerDBus and synchronously initialize it.

Initializing the object will export the debug object on @connection. The object will remain registered until the last reference to the #GDebugControllerDBus is dropped.

Initialization may fail if registering the object on @connection fails.

# Drive in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.Drive.html

`pub struct Drive { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GDrive` represents a piece of hardware connected to the machine.
It’s generally only created for removable hardware or hardware with
removable media. For example, an optical disc drive, or a USB flash drive.

`GDrive` is a container class for [ Volume](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Volume.html) objects that stem from
the same piece of media. As such,

`GDrive` abstracts a drive with
(or without) removable media and provides operations for querying
whether media is available, determining whether media change is
automatically detected and ejecting the media.If the `GDrive` reports that media isn’t automatically detected, one
can poll for media; typically one should not do this periodically
as a poll for media operation is potentially expensive and may
spin up the drive creating noise.

`GDrive` supports starting and stopping drives with authentication
support for the former. This can be used to support a diverse set
of use cases including connecting/disconnecting iSCSI devices,
powering down external disk enclosures and starting/stopping
multi-disk devices such as RAID devices. Note that the actual
semantics and side-effects of starting/stopping a `GDrive` may vary
according to implementation. To choose the correct verbs in e.g. a
file manager, use [ DriveExt::start_stop_type()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DriveExt.html#method.start_stop_type).

For [porting from GnomeVFS](https://gtk-rs.org/migrating-gnome-vfs.html) note that there is no
equivalent of `GDrive` in that API.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#changed)`changed`

Emitted when the drive’s state has changed.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#disconnected)`disconnected`

This signal is emitted when the #GDrive have been disconnected. If the recipient is holding references to the object they should release them so the object can be finalized.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#eject-button)`eject-button`

Emitted when the physical eject button (if any) of a drive has been pressed.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#stop-button)`stop-button`

Emitted when the physical stop button (if any) of a drive has been pressed.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.
