# DtlsClientConnection in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DtlsClientConnection.html

`pub struct DtlsClientConnection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GDtlsClientConnection` is the client-side subclass of
[ DtlsConnection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DtlsConnection.html), representing a client-side DTLS connection.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#accepted-cas)`accepted-cas`

A list of the distinguished names of the Certificate Authorities that the server will accept client certificates signed by. If the server requests a client certificate during the handshake, then this property will be set after the handshake completes.

Each item in the list is a #GByteArray which contains the complete subject DN of the certificate authority.

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#server-identity)`server-identity`

A #GSocketConnectable describing the identity of the server that is expected on the other end of the connection.

If the [ TlsCertificateFlags::BAD_IDENTITY](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.BAD_IDENTITY) flag is set in
#GDtlsClientConnection:validation-flags, this object will be used
to determine the expected identify of the remote end of the
connection; if #GDtlsClientConnection:server-identity is not set,
or does not match the identity presented by the server, then the

[validation will fail.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.BAD_IDENTITY)

`TlsCertificateFlags::BAD_IDENTITY`In addition to its use in verifying the server certificate, this is also used to give a hint to the server about what certificate we expect, which is useful for servers that serve virtual hosts.

Readable | Writable | Construct

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#validation-flags)`validation-flags`

What steps to perform when validating a certificate received from a server. Server certificates that fail to validate in any of the ways indicated here will be rejected unless the application overrides the default via #GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate.

GLib guarantees that if certificate verification fails, at least one
flag will be set, but it does not guarantee that all possible flags
will be set. Accordingly, you may not safely decide to ignore any
particular type of error. For example, it would be incorrect to mask
[ TlsCertificateFlags::EXPIRED](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.EXPIRED) if you want to allow expired certificates,
because this could potentially be the only error flag set even if
other problems exist with the certificate. Therefore, there is no
safe way to use this property. This is not a horrible problem,
though, because you should not be attempting to ignore validation
errors anyway. If you really must ignore TLS certificate errors,
connect to #GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate.

Readable | Writable | Construct

#### DtlsConnection

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#advertised-protocols)`advertised-protocols`

The list of application-layer protocols that the connection advertises that it is willing to speak. See g_dtls_connection_set_advertised_protocols().

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#base-socket)`base-socket`

The #GDatagramBased that the connection wraps. Note that this may be any implementation of #GDatagramBased, not just a #GSocket.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#certificate)`certificate`

The connection’s certificate; see g_dtls_connection_set_certificate().

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#ciphersuite-name)`ciphersuite-name`

The name of the DTLS ciphersuite in use. See g_dtls_connection_get_ciphersuite_name().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#database)`database`

The certificate database to use when verifying this TLS connection. If no certificate database is set, then the default database will be used. See g_tls_backend_get_default_database().

When using a non-default database, #GDtlsConnection must fall back to using the #GTlsDatabase to perform certificate verification using g_tls_database_verify_chain(), which means certificate verification will not be able to make use of TLS session context. This may be less secure. For example, if you create your own #GTlsDatabase that just wraps the default #GTlsDatabase, you might expect that you have not changed anything, but this is not true because you may have altered the behavior of #GDtlsConnection by causing it to use g_tls_database_verify_chain(). See the documentation of g_tls_database_verify_chain() for more details on specific security checks that may not be performed. Accordingly, setting a non-default database is discouraged except for specialty applications with unusual security requirements.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interaction)`interaction`

A #GTlsInteraction object to be used when the connection or certificate database need to interact with the user. This will be used to prompt the user for passwords where necessary.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#negotiated-protocol)`negotiated-protocol`

The application-layer protocol negotiated during the TLS handshake. See g_dtls_connection_get_negotiated_protocol().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#peer-certificate)`peer-certificate`

The connection’s peer’s certificate, after the TLS handshake has completed or failed. Note in particular that this is not yet set during the emission of #GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate.

(You can watch for a #GObject::notify signal on this property to detect when a handshake has occurred.)

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#peer-certificate-errors)`peer-certificate-errors`

The errors noticed while verifying
#GDtlsConnection:peer-certificate. Normally this should be 0, but
it may not be if #GDtlsClientConnection:validation-flags is not
[ TlsCertificateFlags::VALIDATE_ALL](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.VALIDATE_ALL), or if
#GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate overrode the default
behavior.

GLib guarantees that if certificate verification fails, at least
one error will be set, but it does not guarantee that all possible
errors will be set. Accordingly, you may not safely decide to
ignore any particular type of error. For example, it would be
incorrect to mask [ TlsCertificateFlags::EXPIRED](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.EXPIRED) if you want to allow
expired certificates, because this could potentially be the only
error flag set even if other problems exist with the certificate.

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#protocol-version)`protocol-version`

The DTLS protocol version in use. See g_dtls_connection_get_protocol_version().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rehandshake-mode)`rehandshake-mode`

The rehandshaking mode. See g_dtls_connection_set_rehandshake_mode().

Readable | Writable | Construct

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#require-close-notify)`require-close-notify`

Whether or not proper TLS close notification is required. See g_dtls_connection_set_require_close_notify().

Readable | Writable | Construct

# DtlsConnection in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DtlsConnection.html

`pub struct DtlsConnection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GDtlsConnection` is the base DTLS connection class type, which wraps
a [ DatagramBased](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DatagramBased.html) and provides DTLS encryption on top of it. Its
subclasses,

[and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DtlsClientConnection.html)

`DtlsClientConnection`[, implement client-side and server-side DTLS, respectively.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DtlsServerConnection.html)

`DtlsServerConnection`For TLS support, see [ TlsConnection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsConnection.html).

As DTLS is datagram based, `GDtlsConnection` implements
[ DatagramBased](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DatagramBased.html), presenting a datagram-socket-like API for the
encrypted connection. This operates over a base datagram connection, which is
also a

`GDatagramBased` ([).](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DtlsConnection.html#base-socket)

`base-socket`To close a DTLS connection, use [ DtlsConnectionExt::close()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DtlsConnectionExt.html#method.close).

Neither [ DtlsServerConnection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DtlsServerConnection.html) or

[set the peer address on their base](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DtlsClientConnection.html)

`DtlsClientConnection`[if it is a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DatagramBased.html)

`DatagramBased`[— it is up to the caller to do that if they wish. If they do not, and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Socket.html)

`Socket`[is called on the base socket, the](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SocketExt.html#method.close)

`SocketExt::close()``GDtlsConnection` will not raise a `G_IO_ERROR_NOT_CONNECTED` error on
further I/O.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#advertised-protocols)`advertised-protocols`

The list of application-layer protocols that the connection advertises that it is willing to speak. See g_dtls_connection_set_advertised_protocols().

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#base-socket)`base-socket`

The #GDatagramBased that the connection wraps. Note that this may be any implementation of #GDatagramBased, not just a #GSocket.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#certificate)`certificate`

The connection’s certificate; see g_dtls_connection_set_certificate().

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#ciphersuite-name)`ciphersuite-name`

The name of the DTLS ciphersuite in use. See g_dtls_connection_get_ciphersuite_name().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#database)`database`

The certificate database to use when verifying this TLS connection. If no certificate database is set, then the default database will be used. See g_tls_backend_get_default_database().

When using a non-default database, #GDtlsConnection must fall back to using the #GTlsDatabase to perform certificate verification using g_tls_database_verify_chain(), which means certificate verification will not be able to make use of TLS session context. This may be less secure. For example, if you create your own #GTlsDatabase that just wraps the default #GTlsDatabase, you might expect that you have not changed anything, but this is not true because you may have altered the behavior of #GDtlsConnection by causing it to use g_tls_database_verify_chain(). See the documentation of g_tls_database_verify_chain() for more details on specific security checks that may not be performed. Accordingly, setting a non-default database is discouraged except for specialty applications with unusual security requirements.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interaction)`interaction`

A #GTlsInteraction object to be used when the connection or certificate database need to interact with the user. This will be used to prompt the user for passwords where necessary.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#negotiated-protocol)`negotiated-protocol`

The application-layer protocol negotiated during the TLS handshake. See g_dtls_connection_get_negotiated_protocol().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#peer-certificate)`peer-certificate`

The connection’s peer’s certificate, after the TLS handshake has completed or failed. Note in particular that this is not yet set during the emission of #GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate.

(You can watch for a #GObject::notify signal on this property to detect when a handshake has occurred.)

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#peer-certificate-errors)`peer-certificate-errors`

The errors noticed while verifying
#GDtlsConnection:peer-certificate. Normally this should be 0, but
it may not be if #GDtlsClientConnection:validation-flags is not
[ TlsCertificateFlags::VALIDATE_ALL](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.VALIDATE_ALL), or if
#GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate overrode the default
behavior.

GLib guarantees that if certificate verification fails, at least
one error will be set, but it does not guarantee that all possible
errors will be set. Accordingly, you may not safely decide to
ignore any particular type of error. For example, it would be
incorrect to mask [ TlsCertificateFlags::EXPIRED](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.EXPIRED) if you want to allow
expired certificates, because this could potentially be the only
error flag set even if other problems exist with the certificate.

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#protocol-version)`protocol-version`

The DTLS protocol version in use. See g_dtls_connection_get_protocol_version().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rehandshake-mode)`rehandshake-mode`

The rehandshaking mode. See g_dtls_connection_set_rehandshake_mode().

Readable | Writable | Construct

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#require-close-notify)`require-close-notify`

Whether or not proper TLS close notification is required. See g_dtls_connection_set_require_close_notify().

Readable | Writable | Construct

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#accept-certificate)`accept-certificate`

Emitted during the TLS handshake after the peer certificate has been received. You can examine @peer_cert’s certification path by calling g_tls_certificate_get_issuer() on it.

For a client-side connection, @peer_cert is the server’s
certificate, and the signal will only be emitted if the
certificate was not acceptable according to @conn’s
#GDtlsClientConnection:validation_flags. If you would like the
certificate to be accepted despite @errors, return [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) from the
signal handler. Otherwise, if no handler accepts the certificate,
the handshake will fail with

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsError.html#variant.BadCertificate)

`TlsError::BadCertificate`GLib guarantees that if certificate verification fails, this signal
will be emitted with at least one error will be set in @errors, but
it does not guarantee that all possible errors will be set.
Accordingly, you may not safely decide to ignore any particular
type of error. For example, it would be incorrect to ignore
[ TlsCertificateFlags::EXPIRED](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.EXPIRED) if you want to allow expired
certificates, because this could potentially be the only error flag
set even if other problems exist with the certificate.

For a server-side connection, @peer_cert is the certificate
presented by the client, if this was requested via the server’s
#GDtlsServerConnection:authentication_mode. On the server side,
the signal is always emitted when the client presents a
certificate, and the certificate will only be accepted if a
handler returns [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html).

Note that if this signal is emitted as part of asynchronous I/O
in the main thread, then you should not attempt to interact with
the user before returning from the signal handler. If you want to
let the user decide whether or not to accept the certificate, you
would have to return [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) from the signal handler on the first
attempt, and then after the connection attempt returns a

[, you can interact with the user, and if the user decides to accept the certificate, remember that fact, create a new connection, and return](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsError.html#variant.BadCertificate)

`TlsError::BadCertificate`[from the signal handler the next time.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`If you are doing I/O in another thread, you do not need to worry about this, and can simply block in the signal handler until the UI thread returns an answer.

**crate feature**only.

`v2_70`[if the connection has not handshaked or has been closed. Beware that the TLS backend may use any of multiple different naming conventions, because OpenSSL and GnuTLS have their own ciphersuite naming conventions that are different from each other and different from the standard, IANA- registered ciphersuite names. The ciphersuite name is intended to be displayed to the user for informative purposes only, and parsing it is not recommended.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

# DtlsServerConnection in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.DtlsServerConnection.html

`pub struct DtlsServerConnection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GDtlsServerConnection` is the server-side subclass of
[ DtlsConnection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DtlsConnection.html), representing a server-side DTLS connection.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#authentication-mode)`authentication-mode`

The #GTlsAuthenticationMode for the server. This can be changed before calling g_dtls_connection_handshake() if you want to rehandshake with a different mode from the initial handshake.

Readable | Writable

#### DtlsConnection

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#advertised-protocols)`advertised-protocols`

The list of application-layer protocols that the connection advertises that it is willing to speak. See g_dtls_connection_set_advertised_protocols().

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#base-socket)`base-socket`

The #GDatagramBased that the connection wraps. Note that this may be any implementation of #GDatagramBased, not just a #GSocket.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#certificate)`certificate`

The connection’s certificate; see g_dtls_connection_set_certificate().

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#ciphersuite-name)`ciphersuite-name`

The name of the DTLS ciphersuite in use. See g_dtls_connection_get_ciphersuite_name().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#database)`database`

The certificate database to use when verifying this TLS connection. If no certificate database is set, then the default database will be used. See g_tls_backend_get_default_database().

When using a non-default database, #GDtlsConnection must fall back to using the #GTlsDatabase to perform certificate verification using g_tls_database_verify_chain(), which means certificate verification will not be able to make use of TLS session context. This may be less secure. For example, if you create your own #GTlsDatabase that just wraps the default #GTlsDatabase, you might expect that you have not changed anything, but this is not true because you may have altered the behavior of #GDtlsConnection by causing it to use g_tls_database_verify_chain(). See the documentation of g_tls_database_verify_chain() for more details on specific security checks that may not be performed. Accordingly, setting a non-default database is discouraged except for specialty applications with unusual security requirements.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interaction)`interaction`

A #GTlsInteraction object to be used when the connection or certificate database need to interact with the user. This will be used to prompt the user for passwords where necessary.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#negotiated-protocol)`negotiated-protocol`

The application-layer protocol negotiated during the TLS handshake. See g_dtls_connection_get_negotiated_protocol().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#peer-certificate)`peer-certificate`

The connection’s peer’s certificate, after the TLS handshake has completed or failed. Note in particular that this is not yet set during the emission of #GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate.

(You can watch for a #GObject::notify signal on this property to detect when a handshake has occurred.)

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#peer-certificate-errors)`peer-certificate-errors`

The errors noticed while verifying
#GDtlsConnection:peer-certificate. Normally this should be 0, but
it may not be if #GDtlsClientConnection:validation-flags is not
[ TlsCertificateFlags::VALIDATE_ALL](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.VALIDATE_ALL), or if
#GDtlsConnection::accept-certificate overrode the default
behavior.

GLib guarantees that if certificate verification fails, at least
one error will be set, but it does not guarantee that all possible
errors will be set. Accordingly, you may not safely decide to
ignore any particular type of error. For example, it would be
incorrect to mask [ TlsCertificateFlags::EXPIRED](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TlsCertificateFlags.html#associatedconstant.EXPIRED) if you want to allow
expired certificates, because this could potentially be the only
error flag set even if other problems exist with the certificate.

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#protocol-version)`protocol-version`

The DTLS protocol version in use. See g_dtls_connection_get_protocol_version().

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rehandshake-mode)`rehandshake-mode`

The rehandshaking mode. See g_dtls_connection_set_rehandshake_mode().

Readable | Writable | Construct

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#require-close-notify)`require-close-notify`

Whether or not proper TLS close notification is required. See g_dtls_connection_set_require_close_notify().

Readable | Writable | Construct

# Emblem in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.Emblem.html

`pub struct Emblem { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GEmblem` is an implementation of [ Icon](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Icon.html) that supports
having an emblem, which is an icon with additional properties.
It can than be added to a

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.EmblemedIcon.html)

`EmblemedIcon`Currently, only metainformation about the emblem’s origin is supported. More may be added in the future.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#icon)`icon`

The actual icon of the emblem.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#origin)`origin`

The origin the emblem is derived from.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], `IconExt`

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# Icon in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.Icon.html

`pub struct Icon { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GIcon` is a very minimal interface for icons. It provides functions
for checking the equality of two icons, hashing of icons and
serializing an icon to and from strings.

`GIcon` does not provide the actual pixmap for the icon as this is out
of GIO’s scope, however implementations of `GIcon` may contain the name
of an icon (see [ ThemedIcon](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ThemedIcon.html)), or the path to an icon
(see

[).](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LoadableIcon.html)

`LoadableIcon`To obtain a hash of a `GIcon`, see `Gio::Icon::hash()`.

To check if two `GIcon`s are equal, see `Gio::Icon::equal()`.

For serializing a `GIcon`, use [ IconExt::serialize()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.IconExt.html#method.serialize) and

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Icon.html#method.deserialize)

`deserialize()`If you want to consume `GIcon` (for example, in a toolkit) you must
be prepared to handle at least the three following cases:
[ LoadableIcon](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LoadableIcon.html),

[and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ThemedIcon.html)

`ThemedIcon`[. It may also make sense to have fast-paths for other cases (like handling](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.EmblemedIcon.html)

`EmblemedIcon`[directly, for example) but all compliant](https://docs.gtk.org/gdk-pixbuf/class.Pixbuf.html)

`GdkPixbuf``GIcon` implementations outside of GIO must
implement [.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LoadableIcon.html)

`LoadableIcon`If your application or library provides one or more `GIcon`
implementations you need to ensure that your new implementation also
implements [ LoadableIcon](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LoadableIcon.html).  Additionally, you must provide an
implementation of

[that gives a result that is understood by](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.IconExt.html#method.serialize)

`IconExt::serialize()`[, yielding one of the built-in icon types.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Icon.html#method.deserialize)

`deserialize()`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/icon.rs.html#52)

Generate a #GIcon instance from @str. This function can fail if @str is not valid - see g_icon_to_string() for discussion.

If your application or library provides one or more #GIcon implementations you need to ensure that each #GType is registered with the type system prior to calling g_icon_new_for_string().

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#str)`str`

A string obtained via g_icon_to_string().

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

An object implementing the #GIcon
interface or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if @error is set.

# EmblemedIcon in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.EmblemedIcon.html

`pub struct EmblemedIcon { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GEmblemedIcon` is an implementation of [ Icon](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Icon.html) that supports
adding an emblem to an icon. Adding multiple emblems to an
icon is ensured via

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.EmblemedIconExt.html#method.add_emblem)

`EmblemedIconExt::add_emblem()`Note that `GEmblemedIcon` allows no control over the position
of the emblems. See also [ Emblem](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Emblem.html) for more information.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#gicon)`gicon`

The [ Icon](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Icon.html) to attach emblems to.

Readable | Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[ EmblemedIconExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.EmblemedIconExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`],

`IconExt`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/object.rs.html#206)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#method.dynamic_cast)#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/object.rs.html#206)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#method.dynamic_cast)

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# File in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.File.html

`pub struct File { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GFile` is a high level abstraction for manipulating files on a
virtual file system. `GFile`s are lightweight, immutable objects
that do no I/O upon creation. It is necessary to understand that
`GFile` objects do not represent files, merely an identifier for a
file. All file content I/O is implemented as streaming operations
(see [ InputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InputStream.html) and

[).](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.OutputStream.html)

`OutputStream`To construct a `GFile`, you can use:

- `for_path()`
- `for_uri()`
- `for_commandline_arg()`- `for_commandline_arg_and_cwd()`
- `new_tmp()`
- `new_tmp_async()`
- `new_tmp_dir_async()`
- `for_parse_name()`- `FileExt::parse_name()`
- `Gio::File::new_build_filename()`or- `new_build_filenamev()`

One way to think of a `GFile` is as an abstraction of a pathname. For
normal files the system pathname is what is stored internally, but as
`GFile`s are extensible it could also be something else that corresponds
to a pathname in a userspace implementation of a filesystem.

`GFile`s make up hierarchies of directories and files that correspond to
the files on a filesystem. You can move through the file system with
`GFile` using [ FileExt::parent()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.parent) to get an identifier for the
parent directory,

[to get a child within a directory, and](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.child)

`FileExt::child()`[to resolve a relative path between two](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.resolve_relative_path)

`FileExt::resolve_relative_path()``GFile`s. There can be multiple hierarchies, so you may not
end up at the same root if you repeatedly call [on two different files.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.parent)

`FileExt::parent()`All `GFile`s have a basename (get with [ FileExt::basename()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.basename)). These
names are byte strings that are used to identify the file on the filesystem
(relative to its parent directory) and there is no guarantees that they
have any particular charset encoding or even make any sense at all. If
you want to use filenames in a user interface you should use the display
name that you can get by requesting the

`G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_DISPLAY_NAME` attribute with
[. This is guaranteed to be in UTF-8 and can be used in a user interface. But always store the real basename or the](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.query_info)

`FileExt::query_info()``GFile`
to use to actually access the file, because there is no way to go from a
display name to the actual name.Using `GFile` as an identifier has the same weaknesses as using a path
in that there may be multiple aliases for the same file. For instance,
hard or soft links may cause two different `GFile`s to refer to the same
file. Other possible causes for aliases are: case insensitive filesystems,
short and long names on FAT/NTFS, or bind mounts in Linux. If you want to
check if two `GFile`s point to the same file you can query for the
`G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ID_FILE` attribute. Note that `GFile` does some trivial
canonicalization of pathnames passed in, so that trivial differences in
the path string used at creation (duplicated slashes, slash at end of
path, `.` or `..` path segments, etc) does not create different `GFile`s.

Many `GFile` operations have both synchronous and asynchronous versions
to suit your application. Asynchronous versions of synchronous functions
simply have `_async()` appended to their function names. The asynchronous
I/O functions call a `callback::Gio::AsyncReadyCallback which is then used to  finalize the operation, producing a [`AsyncResult`][crate::AsyncResult] which is then  passed to the function’s matching `_finish()` operation.

It is highly recommended to use asynchronous calls when running within a
shared main loop, such as in the main thread of an application. This avoids
I/O operations blocking other sources on the main loop from being dispatched.
Synchronous I/O operations should be performed from worker threads. See the
[introduction to asynchronous programming section](https://gtk-rs.org/overview.html#asynchronous-programming)
for more.

Some `GFile` operations almost always take a noticeable amount of time, and
so do not have synchronous analogs. Notable cases include:

- `FileExt::mount_mountable()`
- `FileExt::unmount_mountable_with_operation()`
- `FileExt::eject_mountable_with_operation()`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#entity-tags)Entity Tags

One notable feature of `GFile`s are entity tags, or ‘etags’ for
short. Entity tags are somewhat like a more abstract version of the
traditional mtime, and can be used to quickly determine if the file
has been modified from the version on the file system. See the
description of HTTP ETags in
[RFC9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-etag).
`GFile` Entity Tags are a very similar concept.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file.rs.html#168-174)#### pub fn [for_commandline_arg](https://gtk-rs.org#method.for_commandline_arg)(arg: impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[OsStr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/ffi/os_str/struct.OsStr.html)>) -> [File](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.File.html)

#### pub fn [for_commandline_arg](https://gtk-rs.org#method.for_commandline_arg)(arg: impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[OsStr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/ffi/os_str/struct.OsStr.html)>) -> [File](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.File.html)

Creates a #GFile with the given argument from the command line. The value of @arg can be either a URI, an absolute path or a relative path resolved relative to the current working directory. This operation never fails, but the returned object might not support any I/O operation if @arg points to a malformed path.

Note that on Windows, this function expects its argument to be in
UTF-8 – not the system code page.  This means that you
should not use this function with string from argv as it is passed
to main().  g_win32_get_command_line() will return a UTF-8 version of
the commandline.  #GApplication also uses UTF-8 but
g_application_command_line_create_file_for_arg() may be more useful
for you there.  It is also always possible to use this function with
#GOptionContext arguments of type [ glib::OptionArg::Filename](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/auto/enums/enum.OptionArg.html#variant.Filename).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#arg)`arg`

a command line string

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

a new #GFile. Free the returned object with g_object_unref().

Creates a #GFile with the given argument from the command line.

This function is similar to g_file_new_for_commandline_arg() except that it allows for passing the current working directory as an argument instead of using the current working directory of the process.

This is useful if the commandline argument was given in a context other than the invocation of the current process.

See also g_application_command_line_create_file_for_arg().

This method is like [ iter](https://gtk-rs.org#method.iter), except only yields bits in contained named flags.
Any unknown bits, or bits not corresponding to a contained flag will not be yielded.

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# FileAttributeMatcher in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html

`pub struct FileAttributeMatcher { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Determines if a string matches a file attribute.

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file_attribute_matcher.rs.html#47-53)#### pub fn [new](https://gtk-rs.org#method.new)(attributes: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [FileAttributeMatcher](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file_attribute_matcher.rs.html#47-53)

#### pub fn [new](https://gtk-rs.org#method.new)(attributes: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [FileAttributeMatcher](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html)

Creates a new file attribute matcher, which matches attributes
against a given string. [GFileAttributeMatchers](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html)[crate::FileAttributeMatcher](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html) are reference
counted structures, and are created with a reference count of 1. If
the number of references falls to 0, the [ FileAttributeMatcher](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html) is
automatically destroyed.

The @attributes string should be formatted with specific keys separated
from namespaces with a double colon. Several `"namespace::key"` strings may be
concatenated with a single comma (e.g. `"standard::type,standard::is-hidden"`).
The wildcard `"*"` may be used to match all keys and namespaces, or
`"namespace::*"` will match all keys in a given namespace.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-of-file-attribute-matcher-strings-and-results)Examples of file attribute matcher strings and results

- `"*"`: matches all attributes.
- `"standard::is-hidden"`: matches only the key is-hidden in the standard namespace.
- `"standard::type,unix::*"`: matches the type key in the standard namespace and all keys in the unix namespace.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#attributes)`attributes`

an attribute string to match.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

a #GFileAttributeMatcher

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file_attribute_matcher.rs.html#69-76)#### pub fn [enumerate_namespace](https://gtk-rs.org#method.enumerate_namespace)(&self, ns: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Checks if the matcher will match all of the keys in a given namespace.
This will always return [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if a wildcard character is in use (e.g. if
matcher was created with “standard::*” and @ns is “standard”, or if matcher was created
using “*” and namespace is anything.)

) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FileAttributeMatcher](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html)>

Subtracts all attributes of @subtract from @self and returns a matcher that supports those attributes.

Note that currently it is not possible to remove a single attribute when the @self matches the whole namespace - or remove a namespace or attribute when the matcher matches everything. This is a limitation of the current implementation, but may be fixed in the future.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#subtract)`subtract`

The matcher to subtract

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-4)Returns

A file attribute matcher matching all attributes of @self that are not matched by @subtract

Prints what the matcher is matching against. The format will be equal to the format passed to g_file_attribute_matcher_new(). The output however, might not be identical, as the matcher may decide to use a different order or omit needless parts.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-5)Returns

a string describing the attributes the matcher matches
against or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if @self was

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

#### pub const [REPLACE_DESTINATION](https://gtk-rs.org#associatedconstant.REPLACE_DESTINATION): Self

Replace the destination as if it didn’t exist before. Don’t try to keep any old permissions, replace instead of following links. This is generally useful if you’re doing a “copy over” rather than a “save new version of” replace operation. You can think of it as “unlink destination” before writing to it, although the implementation may not be exactly like that. This flag can only be used with g_file_replace() and its variants, including g_file_replace_contents(). Since 2.20

#### fn [sub_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/arith/trait.SubAssign.html#tymethod.sub_assign)(&mut self, other: Self)

The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# FileEnumerator in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.FileEnumerator.html

`pub struct FileEnumerator { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GFileEnumerator` allows you to operate on a set of [ File](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.File.html) objects,
returning a

[structure for each file enumerated (e.g.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html)

`FileInfo`[will return a](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.enumerate_children)

`FileExt::enumerate_children()``GFileEnumerator` for each
of the children within a directory).To get the next file’s information from a `GFileEnumerator`, use
[ FileEnumeratorExt::next_file()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileEnumeratorExt.html#method.next_file) or its asynchronous version,

[. Note that the asynchronous version will return a list of](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileEnumeratorExt.html#method.next_files_async)

`FileEnumeratorExt::next_files_async()`[objects, whereas the synchronous will only return the next file in the enumerator.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html)

`FileInfo`The ordering of returned files is unspecified for non-Unix
platforms; for more information, see `GLib::Dir::read_name()`.  On Unix,
when operating on local files, returned files will be sorted by
inode number.  Effectively you can assume that the ordering of
returned files will be stable between successive calls (and
applications) assuming the directory is unchanged.

If your application needs a specific ordering, such as by name or modification time, you will have to implement that in your application code.

To close a `GFileEnumerator`, use [ FileEnumeratorExtManual::close()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileEnumeratorExtManual.html#method.close), or
its asynchronous version,

[. Once a](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileEnumeratorExt.html#method.close_async)

`FileEnumeratorExt::close_async()``GFileEnumerator` is closed, no further actions may be performed
on it, and it should be freed with `GObject::Object::unref()`.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#container)`container`

The container that is being enumerated.

Writable | Construct Only

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[ FileEnumeratorExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileEnumeratorExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`],

`FileEnumeratorExtManual`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will

# FileInfo in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.FileInfo.html

`pub struct FileInfo { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Stores information about a file system object referenced by a [ File](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.File.html).

Functionality for manipulating basic metadata for files. `GFileInfo`
implements methods for getting information that all files should
contain, and allows for manipulation of extended attributes.

See the [file attributes](https://gtk-rs.org/file-attributes.html) document for more
information on how GIO handles file attributes.

To obtain a `GFileInfo` for a [ File](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.File.html), use

[(or its async variant). To obtain a](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.query_info)

`FileExt::query_info()``GFileInfo`
for a file input or output stream, use [or](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileInputStreamExt.html#method.query_info)

`FileInputStreamExt::query_info()`[(or their async variants).](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileOutputStreamExt.html#method.query_info)

`FileOutputStreamExt::query_info()`To change the actual attributes of a file, you should then set the
attribute in the `GFileInfo` and call [ FileExt::set_attributes_from_info()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.set_attributes_from_info)
or

[on a](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.set_attributes_async)

`FileExt::set_attributes_async()``GFile`.However, not all attributes can be changed in the file. For instance,
the actual size of a file cannot be changed via [ set_size()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html#method.set_size).
You may call

[and](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.query_settable_attributes)

`FileExt::query_settable_attributes()`[to discover the settable attributes of a particular file at runtime.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.query_writable_namespaces)

`FileExt::query_writable_namespaces()`The direct accessors, such as [ name()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html#method.name), are slightly more
optimized than the generic attribute accessors, such as

[.This optimization will matter only if calling the API in a tight loop.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html#method.attribute_byte_string)

`attribute_byte_string()`It is an error to call these accessors without specifying their required file
attributes when creating the `GFileInfo`. Use
[ has_attribute()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html#method.has_attribute) or

[to check what attributes are specified for a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html#method.list_attributes)

`list_attributes()``GFileInfo`.[ FileAttributeMatcher](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileAttributeMatcher.html) allows for searching through a

`GFileInfo`
for attributes.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[`trait@glib::ObjectExt`]

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

Gets the value of an attribute, formatted as a human readable string.

This escapes things as needed to make the string valid UTF-8 and readable by humans. It’s not meant to be a machine readable or reversible escaping format.

To format file name attributes of type
[enum@Gio.FileAttributeType.BYTE_STRING] for output as UTF-8, use
`filename_to_utf8()` instead:
**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

```
const char *trash_orig_path_byte_string;
g_autofree char *trash_orig_path_utf8 = NULL;
trash_orig_path_byte_string = g_file_info_get_attribute_byte_string (info, G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TRASH_ORIG_PATH);
trash_orig_path_utf8 = g_filename_to_utf8 (trash_orig_path_byte_string, -1, NULL, NULL, NULL);
if (trash_orig_path_utf8 != NULL)
  g_message ("Some larger UTF-8 string with filename embedded as %s", trash_orig_path_utf8);
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#attribute-3)`attribute`

a file attribute key.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-5)Returns

a UTF-8 string associated with the given @attribute, or
[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the attribute wasn’t set.
When you’re done with the string it must be freed with g_free().

#### fn [append_to](https://gtk-rs.org#method.append_to)(
    &self,
    flags: [FileCreateFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCreateFlags.html),
    cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Cancellable.html)>>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FileOutputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileOutputStream.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Gets an output stream for appending data to the file. If the file doesn’t already exist it is created.

By default files created are generally readable by everyone,
but if you pass [ FileCreateFlags::PRIVATE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCreateFlags.html#associatedconstant.PRIVATE) in @flags the file
will be made readable only to the current user, to the level that
is supported on the target filesystem.

If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled
by triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the
operation was cancelled, the error

[will be returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Cancelled)

`IOErrorEnum::Cancelled`Some file systems don’t allow all file names, and may return an
[ IOErrorEnum::InvalidFilename](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.InvalidFilename) error. If the file is a directory the

[error will be returned. Other errors are possible too, and depend on what kind of filesystem the file is on.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.IsDirectory)

`IOErrorEnum::IsDirectory`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#flags)`flags`

a set of #GFileCreateFlags

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#cancellable)`cancellable`

optional #GCancellable object,
[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) to ignore

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

a #GFileOutputStream, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on error.
Free the returned object with g_object_unref().

Copies the file attributes from @self to @destination.

Normally only a subset of the file attributes are copied,
those that are copies in a normal file copy operation
(which for instance does not include e.g. owner). However
if [ FileCopyFlags::ALL_METADATA](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCopyFlags.html#associatedconstant.ALL_METADATA) is specified in @flags, then
all the metadata that is possible to copy is copied. This
is useful when implementing move by copy + delete source.

Creates a new file and returns an output stream for writing to it. The file must not already exist.

By default files created are generally readable by everyone,
but if you pass [ FileCreateFlags::PRIVATE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCreateFlags.html#associatedconstant.PRIVATE) in @flags the file
will be made readable only to the current user, to the level
that is supported on the target filesystem.

by triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the
operation was cancelled, the error

[will be returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Cancelled)

`IOErrorEnum::Cancelled`If a file or directory with this name already exists the
[ IOErrorEnum::Exists](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Exists) error will be returned. Some file systems don’t
allow all file names, and may return an

[error, and if the name is to long](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.InvalidFilename)

`IOErrorEnum::InvalidFilename`[will be returned. Other errors are possible too, and depend on what kind of filesystem the file is on.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.FilenameTooLong)

#### fn [create_readwrite](https://gtk-rs.org#method.create_readwrite)(
    &self,

    cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Cancellable.html)>>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FileIOStream](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileIOStream.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Creates a new file and returns a stream for reading and writing to it. The file must not already exist.

By default files created are generally readable by everyone,
but if you pass [ FileCreateFlags::PRIVATE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCreateFlags.html#associatedconstant.PRIVATE) in @flags the file
will be made readable only to the current user, to the level
that is supported on the target filesystem.

If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled
by triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the
operation was cancelled, the error

[will be returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Cancelled)

`IOErrorEnum::Cancelled`If a file or directory with this name already exists, the
[ IOErrorEnum::Exists](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Exists) error will be returned. Some file systems don’t
allow all file names, and may return an

[error, and if the name is too long,](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.InvalidFilename)

`IOErrorEnum::InvalidFilename`[will be returned. Other errors are possible too, and depend on what kind of filesystem the file is on.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.FilenameTooLong)

`IOErrorEnum::FilenameTooLong`Note that in many non-local file cases read and write streams are not supported, so make sure you really need to do read and write streaming, rather than just opening for reading or writing.

Deletes a file. If the @self is a directory, it will only be deleted if it is empty. This has the same semantics as g_unlink().

If @self doesn’t exist, [ IOErrorEnum::NotFound](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.NotFound) will be returned. This allows
for deletion to be implemented avoiding

[time-of-check to time-of-use races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time-of-check_to_time-of-use):

```
g_autoptr(GError) local_error = NULL;
if (!g_file_delete (my_file, my_cancellable, &local_error) &&
    !g_error_matches (local_error, G_IO_ERROR, G_IO_ERROR_NOT_FOUND))
  {
    // deletion failed for some reason other than the file not existing:
    // so report the error
    g_warning ("Failed to delete %s: %s",
               g_file_peek_path (my_file), local_error->message);
  }
```
If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled by
triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the operation
was cancelled, the error

[will be returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Cancelled)

Duplicates a #GFile handle. This operation does not duplicate the actual file or directory represented by the #GFile; see g_file_copy() if attempting to copy a file.

g_file_dup() is useful when a second handle is needed to the same underlying file, for use in a separate thread (#GFile is not thread-safe). For use within the same thread, use g_object_ref() to increment the existing object’s reference count.

This call does no blocking I/O.

Gets the requested information about the files in a directory.
The result is a [ FileEnumerator](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileEnumerator.html) object that will give out

[objects for all the files in the directory.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html)

`FileInfo`The @attributes value is a string that specifies the file
attributes that should be gathered. It is not an error if
it’s not possible to read a particular requested attribute
from a file - it just won’t be set. @attributes should
be a comma-separated list of attributes or attribute wildcards.
The wildcard `*` means all attributes, and a wildcard like
`"standard::*"` means all attributes in the standard namespace.
An example attribute query be `"standard::*,owner::user"`.
The standard attributes are available as defines, like
`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_NAME`. `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_NAME` should
always be specified if you plan to call [ FileEnumeratorExt::child()](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.FileEnumeratorExt.html#method.child) or

`FileEnumerator::iterate()` on the returned enumerator.If @cancellable is not `NULL`, then the operation can be cancelled
by triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the
operation was cancelled, the error [error@Gio.IOErrorEnum.CANCELLED] will be
returned.

If the file does not exist, the [error@Gio.IOErrorEnum.NOT_FOUND] error will be returned. If the file is not a directory, the [error@Gio.IOErrorEnum.NOT_DIRECTORY] error will be returned. Other errors are possible too.

Gets the base name (the last component of the path) for a given #GFile.

If called for the top level of a system (such as the filesystem root or a uri like sftp://host/) it will return a single directory separator (and on Windows, possibly a drive letter).

The base name is a byte string (not UTF-8). It has no defined encoding
or rules other than it may not contain zero bytes.  If you want to use
filenames in a user interface you should use the display name that you
can get by requesting the [ FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_DISPLAY_NAME](https://gtk-rs.org/static.FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_DISPLAY_NAME.html)
attribute with g_file_query_info().

This is generally used to show the #GFile as a nice full-pathname kind of string in a user interface, like in a location entry.

Checks whether @self has the prefix specified by @prefix.

In other words, if the names of initial elements of @self’s pathname match @prefix. Only full pathname elements are matched, so a path like /foo is not considered a prefix of /foobar, only of /foo/bar.

A #GFile is not a prefix of itself. If you want to check for equality, use g_file_equal().

This call does no I/O, as it works purely on names. As such it can
sometimes return [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) even if @self is inside a @prefix (from a
filesystem point of view), because the prefix of @self is an alias
of @prefix.

`false`Checks to see if a file is native to the platform.

A native file is one expressed in the platform-native filename format, e.g. “C:\Windows” or “/usr/bin/”. This does not mean the file is local, as it might be on a locally mounted remote filesystem.

On some systems non-native files may be available using the native
filesystem via a userspace filesystem (FUSE), in these cases this call
will return [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), but g_file_get_path() will still return a native path.

Recursively measures the disk usage of @self.

This is essentially an analog of the ‘du’ command, but it also reports the number of directories and non-directory files encountered (including things like symbolic links).

By default, errors are only reported against the toplevel file
itself.  Errors found while recursing are silently ignored, unless
[ FileMeasureFlags::REPORT_ANY_ERROR](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileMeasureFlags.html#associatedconstant.REPORT_ANY_ERROR) is given in @flags.

The returned size, @disk_usage, is in bytes and should be formatted with g_format_size() in order to get something reasonable for showing in a user interface.

@progress_callback and @progress_data can be given to request periodic progress updates while scanning. See the documentation for #GFileMeasureProgressCallback for information about when and how the callback will be invoked.

Tries to move the file or directory @self to the location specified by @destination. If native move operations are supported then this is used, otherwise a copy + delete fallback is used. The native implementation may support moving directories (for instance on moves inside the same filesystem), but the fallback code does not.

If the flag [ FileCopyFlags::OVERWRITE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCopyFlags.html#associatedconstant.OVERWRITE) is specified an already
existing @destination file is overwritten.

If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled by
triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the operation
was cancelled, the error

by setting this to a #GFileProgressCallback function.
@progress_callback_data will be passed to this function. It is
guaranteed that this callback will be called after all data has been
transferred with the total number of bytes copied during the operation.

If the @self file does not exist, then the [ IOErrorEnum::NotFound](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.NotFound)
error is returned, independent on the status of the @destination.

If [ FileCopyFlags::OVERWRITE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCopyFlags.html#associatedconstant.OVERWRITE) is not specified and the target exists,
then the error

[is returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Exists)

`IOErrorEnum::Exists`If trying to overwrite a file over a directory, the [ IOErrorEnum::IsDirectory](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.IsDirectory)
error is returned. If trying to overwrite a directory with a directory the

[error is returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.WouldMerge)

`IOErrorEnum::WouldMerge`If the source is a directory and the target does not exist, or
[ FileCopyFlags::OVERWRITE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCopyFlags.html#associatedconstant.OVERWRITE) is specified and the target is a file, then
the

[error may be returned (if the native move operation isn’t available).](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.WouldRecurse)

`v2_60`[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file.rs.html#2743-2750)#### fn [query_exists](https://gtk-rs.org#method.query_exists)(&self, cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Cancellable.html)>>) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file.rs.html#2743-2750)

#### fn [query_exists](https://gtk-rs.org#method.query_exists)(&self, cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Cancellable.html)>>) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Utility function to check if a particular file exists.

The fallback implementation of this API is using [ query_info()](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.FileExt.html#method.query_info)
and therefore may do blocking I/O. To asynchronously query the existence
of a file, use

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.FileExt.html#method.query_info_async)

`query_info_async()`Note that in many cases it is [racy to first check for file existence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_of_check_to_time_of_use)
and then execute something based on the outcome of that, because the
file might have been created or removed in between the operations. The
general approach to handling that is to not check, but just do the
operation and handle the errors as they come.

As an example of race-free checking, take the case of reading a file,
and if it doesn’t exist, creating it. There are two racy versions: read
it, and on error create it; and: check if it exists, if not create it.
These can both result in two processes creating the file (with perhaps
a partially written file as the result). The correct approach is to
always try to create the file with g_file_create() which will either
atomically create the file or fail with a [ IOErrorEnum::Exists](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Exists) error.

However, in many cases an existence check is useful in a user interface, for instance to make a menu item sensitive/insensitive, so that you don’t have to fool users that something is possible and then just show an error dialog. If you do this, you should make sure to also handle the errors that can happen due to races when you execute the operation.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file.rs.html#2993-3014)#### fn [query_info](https://gtk-rs.org#method.query_info)(

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gio/auto/file.rs.html#2993-3014)

#### fn [query_info](https://gtk-rs.org#method.query_info)(
    &self,
    attributes: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    flags: [FileQueryInfoFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileQueryInfoFlags.html),
    cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Cancellable.html)>>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FileInfo](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Gets the requested information about specified @self.

The result is a [ FileInfo](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html) object that contains key-value
attributes (such as the type or size of the file).

The @attributes value is a string that specifies the file
attributes that should be gathered. It is not an error if
it’s not possible to read a particular requested attribute
from a file — it just won’t be set. In particular this means that if a file
is inaccessible (due to being in a folder with restrictive permissions), for
example, you can expect the returned [ FileInfo](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html) to have very few
attributes set. You should check whether an attribute is set using

[before trying to retrieve its value.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html#method.has_attribute)

`FileInfo::has_attribute()`It is guaranteed that if any of the following attributes are listed in
@attributes, they will always be set in the returned [ FileInfo](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileInfo.html),
even if the user doesn’t have permissions to access the file:

- `Gio::FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_NAME`
- `Gio::FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_DISPLAY_NAME`

@attributes should be a comma-separated list of attributes or attribute
wildcards. The wildcard `"\*"` means all attributes, and a wildcard like
`"standard::*"` means all attributes in the standard namespace.
An example attribute query might be `"standard::*,owner::user"`.
The standard attributes are available as defines, like
`Gio::FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_NAME`.

If @cancellable is not `NULL`, then the operation can be cancelled
by triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the
operation was cancelled, the error [error@Gio.IOErrorEnum.CANCELLED] will be
returned.

For symlinks, normally the information about the target of the symlink is returned, rather than information about the symlink itself. However if you pass [flags@Gio.FileQueryInfoFlags.NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS] in @flags the information about the symlink itself will be returned. Also, for symlinks that point to non-existing files the information about the symlink itself will be returned.

If the file does not exist, the [error@Gio.IOErrorEnum.NOT_FOUND] error will be returned. Other errors are possible too, and depend on what kind of file system the file is on.

Returns an output stream for overwriting the file, possibly creating a backup copy of the file first. If the file doesn’t exist, it will be created.

This will try to replace the file in the safest way possible so that any errors during the writing will not affect an already existing copy of the file. For instance, for local files it may write to a temporary file and then atomically rename over the destination when the stream is closed.

By default files created are generally readable by everyone,
but if you pass [ FileCreateFlags::PRIVATE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileCreateFlags.html#associatedconstant.PRIVATE) in @flags the file
will be made readable only to the current user, to the level that
is supported on the target filesystem.

If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled
by triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the
operation was cancelled, the error

[will be returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Cancelled)

`IOErrorEnum::Cancelled`If you pass in a non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) @etag value and @self already exists, then
this value is compared to the current entity tag of the file, and if
they differ an

[error is returned. This generally means that the file has been changed since you last read it. You can get the new etag from g_file_output_stream_get_etag() after you’ve finished writing and closed the #GFileOutputStream. When you load a new file you can use g_file_input_stream_query_info() to get the etag of the file.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.WrongEtag)

`IOErrorEnum::WrongEtag`If @make_backup is [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), this function will attempt to make a
backup of the current file before overwriting it. If this fails
a

[error will be returned. If you want to replace anyway, try again with @make_backup set to](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.CantCreateBackup)

`IOErrorEnum::CantCreateBackup`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`If the file is a directory the [ IOErrorEnum::IsDirectory](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.IsDirectory) error will
be returned, and if the file is some other form of non-regular file
then a

[error will be returned. Some file systems don’t allow all file names, and may return an](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.NotRegularFile)

`IOErrorEnum::NotRegularFile`[error, and if the name is to long](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.InvalidFilename)

`IOErrorEnum::InvalidFilename`[will be returned. Other errors are possible too, and depend on what kind of filesystem the file is on.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.FilenameTooLong)

used when replacing local files’ contents.

If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled by
triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the operation
was cancelled, the error

[will be returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.Cancelled)

`IOErrorEnum::Cancelled`The returned @new_etag can be used to verify that the file hasn’t changed the next time it is saved over.

or `None`

Returns an output stream for overwriting the file in readwrite mode, possibly creating a backup copy of the file first. If the file doesn’t exist, it will be created.

For details about the behaviour, see g_file_replace() which does the same thing but returns an output stream only.

Note that in many non-local file cases read and write streams are not supported, so make sure you really need to do read and write streaming, rather than just opening for reading or writing.

Renames @self to the specified display name.

The display name is converted from UTF-8 to the correct encoding for the target filesystem if possible and the @self is renamed to this.

If you want to implement a rename operation in the user interface the
edit name ([ FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_EDIT_NAME](https://gtk-rs.org/static.FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_EDIT_NAME.html)) should be used as the
initial value in the rename widget, and then the result after editing
should be passed to g_file_set_display_name().

On success the resulting converted filename is returned.

If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled by
triggering the cancellable object from another thread. If the operation
was cancelled, the error

(see [`glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()])
If this returns [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), you cannot perform asynchronous operations on
@self in a thread that has a thread-default context.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-52)Returns

Whether or not @self supports thread-default contexts.

Sends @self to the “Trashcan”, if possible. This is similar to
deleting it, but the user can recover it before emptying the trashcan.
Trashing is disabled for system mounts by default (see
g_unix_mount_entry_is_system_internal()), so this call can return the
[ IOErrorEnum::NotSupported](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IOErrorEnum.html#variant.NotSupported) error. Since GLib 2.66, the

`x-gvfs-notrash` unix
mount option can be used to disable g_file_trash() support for particular

`IOErrorEnum::NotSupported``x-gvfs-trash` unix mount option can be used to enable
g_file_trash() support for particular system mounts.If @cancellable is not [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then the operation can be cancelled by

# FileIOStream in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.FileIOStream.html

`pub struct FileIOStream { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GFileIOStream` provides I/O streams that both read and write to the same
file handle.

`GFileIOStream` implements [ Seekable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Seekable.html), which allows the I/O
stream to jump to arbitrary positions in the file and to truncate
the file, provided the filesystem of the file supports these
operations.

To find the position of a file I/O stream, use [ SeekableExt::tell()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SeekableExt.html#method.tell).

To find out if a file I/O stream supports seeking, use
[ SeekableExt::can_seek()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SeekableExt.html#method.can_seek). To position a file I/O stream, use

[. To find out if a file I/O stream supports truncating, use](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SeekableExt.html#method.seek)

`SeekableExt::seek()`[. To truncate a file I/O stream, use](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SeekableExt.html#method.can_truncate)

`SeekableExt::can_truncate()`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SeekableExt.html#method.truncate)

`SeekableExt::truncate()`The default implementation of all the `GFileIOStream` operations
and the implementation of [ Seekable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Seekable.html) just call into the same
operations on the output stream.

`pub struct FileIcon { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GFileIcon` specifies an icon by pointing to an image file
to be used as icon.

It implements [ LoadableIcon](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LoadableIcon.html).

# FileInputStream in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.FileInputStream.html

`pub struct FileInputStream { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GFileInputStream` provides input streams that take their
content from a file.

`GFileInputStream` implements [ Seekable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Seekable.html), which allows the input
stream to jump to arbitrary positions in the file, provided the
filesystem of the file allows it. To find the position of a file
input stream, use

[. To find out if a file input stream supports seeking, use](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SeekableExt.html#method.tell)

`SeekableExt::tell()``vfunc::Gio::Seekable::can_seek`.
To position a file input stream, use `vfunc::Gio::Seekable::seek`.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[ FileInputStreamExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileInputStreamExt.html),

[, [](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.InputStreamExt.html)

`InputStreamExt``trait@glib::ObjectExt`], [,](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.SeekableExt.html)

`SeekableExt`

`InputStreamExtManual`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

Tally usage based on apparent file
sizes.  Normally, the block-size is used, if available, as this is a
more accurate representation of disk space used.
Compare with `du --apparent-size`.
Since GLib 2.78. and similarly to `du` since GNU Coreutils 9.2, this will
ignore the sizes of file types other than regular files and links, as the
sizes of other file types are not specified in a standard way.

Get the underlying bits value.

#### fn [sub_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/arith/trait.SubAssign.html#tymethod.sub_assign)(&mut self, other: Self)

The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# FileMonitor in gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/struct.FileMonitor.html

`pub struct FileMonitor { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Monitors a file or directory for changes.

To obtain a `GFileMonitor` for a file or directory, use
[ FileExt::monitor()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.monitor),

[, or](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.monitor_file)

`FileExt::monitor_file()`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FileExt.html#method.monitor_directory)

`FileExt::monitor_directory()`To get informed about changes to the file or directory you are
monitoring, connect to the [ changed](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileMonitor.html#changed) signal. The
signal will be emitted in the thread-default main context (see
[

`glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()]) of the thread that the monitor
was created in (though if the global default main context is blocked, this
may cause notifications to be blocked even if the thread-default
context is still running).This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#cancelled)`cancelled`

Whether the monitor has been cancelled.

Readable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rate-limit)`rate-limit`

The limit of the monitor to watch for changes, in milliseconds.

Readable | Writable

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#changed)`changed`

Emitted when @file has been changed.

If using [ FileMonitorFlags::WATCH_MOVES](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileMonitorFlags.html#associatedconstant.WATCH_MOVES) on a directory monitor, and
the information is available (and if supported by the backend),
@event_type may be

[,](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.Renamed)

`FileMonitorEvent::Renamed`[or](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.MovedIn)

`FileMonitorEvent::MovedIn`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.MovedOut)

`FileMonitorEvent::MovedOut`In all cases @file will be a child of the monitored directory. For renames, @file will be the old name and @other_file is the new name. For “moved in” events, @file is the name of the file that appeared and @other_file is the old name that it was moved from (in another directory). For “moved out” events, @file is the name of the file that used to be in this directory and @other_file is the name of the file at its new location.

It makes sense to treat [ FileMonitorEvent::MovedIn](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.MovedIn) as
equivalent to

[and](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.Created)

`FileMonitorEvent::Created`[as equivalent to](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.MovedOut)

`FileMonitorEvent::MovedOut`[, with extra information.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.Deleted)

`FileMonitorEvent::Deleted`[is equivalent to a delete/create pair. This is exactly how the events will be reported in the case that the](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.Renamed)

`FileMonitorEvent::Renamed`[flag is not in use.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileMonitorFlags.html#associatedconstant.WATCH_MOVES)

`FileMonitorFlags::WATCH_MOVES`If using the deprecated flag [ FileMonitorFlags::SEND_MOVED](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileMonitorFlags.html#associatedconstant.SEND_MOVED) flag and @event_type is

[, @file will be set to a #GFile containing the old path, and @other_file will be set to a #GFile containing the new path.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileMonitorEvent.html#variant.Moved)

`FileMonitorEvent::Moved`In all the other cases, @other_file will be set to #NULL.

# FileMonitorFlags in gio - Rust
